title: Add type-aware website linting and reduce any usage
description:
The website already compiles with Astro's strict TypeScript config, but the lint layer is still much looser than the typechecker:
- `website/tsconfig.json` extends `astro/tsconfigs/strict`
- `website/eslint.config.mjs` only enables core JS rules plus `eslint-plugin-astro` recommended
- There is no `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` config, so there are no type-aware rules such as `no-explicit-any`, `no-unsafe-assignment`, or `consistent-type-imports`

A quick scan during the Python lint-tightening pass found the current gap is real, not hypothetical:
- 18 `as any` sites in the website tree
- many additional `any` annotations concentrated in `website/src/pages/season/[season]/results.astro`, `website/src/pages/index.astro`, and `website/src/pages/internals.astro`
- the only `eslint-disable` directive is in generated `src/types/game-export.d.ts`, which is already ignored by ESLint, so stale inline disables are not the main problem

Suggested fix:
1. Add `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` and enable the recommended type-checked config for `*.ts` and `*.astro` where practical.
2. Start with a narrow first pass: `no-explicit-any`, `no-unsafe-assignment`, `no-unsafe-member-access`, and `consistent-type-imports`.
3. Clean up the large `.astro` pages incrementally instead of trying to erase all `any` usage in one change.

This should make website regressions show up in lint instead of relying on runtime rendering and manual review.
